candidate_measurements.hypothesis: TILE_COLS=4 launches four blocks per 16-column tile and each reads the whole tile, so the family re-reads its weights 4x (2x for TILE_COLS=8). If that re-read were the limit, col8 would win.
candidate_measurements.method: temporarily routed the registered col4 variant body at the col8 launcher, then re-ran the same census
candidate_measurements.verdict: rejected: col8 is 15% slower on the Q5_K rowtile and 1.7% slower end to end
candidate_measurements.interpretation: The tile re-read is served by L2 and is not the limit. col4 wins because it launches twice as many blocks, so the family is parallelism-limited rather than L2-bandwidth-limited.

candidate_measurements.hypothesis: Each lane issues eight scalar BF16 activation loads per (row, blk); replacing them with one 16-byte load should cut load issue pressure in a kernel that is not at its roofline.
candidate_measurements.method: added a bf16_load8 helper (one uint4 load per lane window) to all three local32 owners, then re-ran scripts/gguf_iq_local32_rows_headroom.py on the same four real IQ4_XS tensors
candidate_measurements.verdict: rejected as neutral: -1.9% on the sibling and +1.5% on the rows==1 owner, both inside run-to-run spread
candidate_measurements.interpretation: The compiler already coalesces the contiguous scalar loads, so the family is not load-issue-bound. Together with the col8 result this localises the remaining headroom to memory-level parallelism at fixed occupancy.

closed_candidates.evidence: qk_t16_selected_direct_gemv is 0.367 ms/step (0.78% of the UD-Q4_K_M verifier) and 0.662 ms/step (1.46% of UD-Q4_K_S)
closed_candidates.verdict: no material lever at verifier rows

closed_candidates.evidence: the Q5_K gate/up dual runs the WMMA prefill owner at verifier rows (5.68 ms/step UD-Q4_K_M); the pair total is 6.38 ms/step against the plain Q4_K dual rowtile's 8.85 ms/step, so UD's gate/up arm is already the cheaper one
closed_candidates.verdict: already the cheapest measured arm; no action

closed_candidates.candidate: Q5/Q6 compact residency and raw consumer qualification
closed_candidates.evidence: Q6_K col8 is 0.77 ms/step in UD against 6.23 ms/step in plain Q4_K_M; Q5_K residency is the col4 rowtile measured above
closed_candidates.verdict: UD is already cheaper than the plain control on both

closed_candidates.evidence: Q3_K has no rows==1 local32 owner, so it has no rows 2-4 sibling. Routing it was measured on gfx1151 at +176.5 tok/s but moved the calibrated mean KL 0.000827 -> 0.001061, 6% over the 1e-3 limit (hipengine/kernels/hip_gfx1100/__init__.py, GGUF_IQ_DENSE_VERIFY_POLICY comment)
closed_candidates.verdict: blocked on the calibrated mean-KL gate; the strict per-row GEMV stays the owner

closed_candidates.candidate: Norm, SiLU, residual, and logits tail
closed_candidates.evidence: rounded_add_rmsnorm 0.836 + add_rmsnorm 0.770 + silu_mul_separate 0.104 + full_attn_gate_mul 0.102 + head rmsnorm 0.073 ms/step = 1.885 ms/step (4.00% of the UD-Q4_K_M verifier)
closed_candidates.verdict: below the repair threshold at verifier rows

open_candidates.candidate: IQ4_XS local32 rows decoder memory access
open_candidates.evidence: 12.24 ms/step, 26.0% of the UD-Q4_K_M verifier, at 46% (ffn_gate, N=17408 K=5120) and 58% (ffn_down, N=5120 K=17408) of the 960 GB/s DRAM roofline
open_candidates.blocker: two scoped instruction-level changes were neutral-to-negative, so the lever is memory-level parallelism at fixed occupancy (prefetch or a wider row/wave split). Both change the block geometry and need a hardware-counter unit plus a new bit-exactness contract.

open_candidates.evidence: 9.23 ms/step, 19.6% of the UD-Q4_K_M verifier; 85.5 us/call for N=5120 K=6144 at 1280 blocks, and 59.1 us/call for the same shape in plain Q4_K_M
open_candidates.blocker: col8 (fewer, fatter blocks) is worse, so the family wants more concurrent blocks or a split-K reduction. Split-K changes the per-output accumulation order, which docs/UD-GFX1151-OPTIMIZE.md already names as the dominant AR-versus-verifier drift source, so it owes the full production profile gate rather than a bit-exactness screen.

open_candidates.evidence: 5.25 ms/step of host residual against 1032 kernel calls/step (5.09 us per launch); the plain control has 824 calls/step, 4.39 ms/step residual and 5.33 us per launch
open_candidates.blocker: reducing it means fewer, wider launches or replay-side launch elision, which is a scheduler/graph-ownership unit rather than a kernel unit.
